title: GetOrphanNodeIds returns truncated object IDs
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5.1 (Mono)

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono unknown - EndeavourOS #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 13 Dec 2025 18:23:21 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER (nvidia; 580.119.02) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.53 GiB memory

### Issue description

Calling `Node.GetOrphanNodeIds` returns an array of int, which appear to be truncated 64-bit IDs. For parity with `GetInstanceID`, it should probably should return an array of ulong instead.

All instance ID-based functions such as `Node.IsInstanceIdValid` and `InstanceFromId` require a ulong ID, which renders the int IDs mostly useless unless you attempt to guess the stripped bits.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a new node outside of the tree or use RemoveChild to orphan an existing one.
- Compare the ID's reported from `node.GetInstanceId` and `Node.GetOrphanNodeIds`. The orphaned IDs are simply the latter half of the full 64-bit ID, presumably from a narrowing conversion.

The MRP does this for both an in-scene node and a runtime node, then prints the IDs and binary representation into the console for easy comparison.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[Mono ID Truncation.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24271890/Mono.ID.Truncation.zip)
